preseason_hypothesis: McDaniel's run-pass marriage will materially reduce pure dropback pressure without eliminating intermediate and deep attempts
confirming_evidence: lower pressure and sack rates; regular play action; five eligible receivers releasing; sustained intermediate and deep concepts
disconfirming_evidence: pressure remains near 2025 levels; heavy max protection; route menu contracts to quick throws
review_trigger: each preseason game and first two regular-season games

preseason_hypothesis: Slater-left guard-Slaughter-Strange-Alt is the leading revised opening-five projection after Biadasz moved to season-ending injured reserve
confirming_evidence: Slaughter takes stable first-unit center work; a clear left-guard winner emerges; stunt and pressure communication stays clean
disconfirming_evidence: another center displaces Slaughter; continued left-guard rotation; repeated assignment errors or additional injury
review_trigger: every first-team practice and the final preseason game

preseason_hypothesis: The new timing and footwork will improve Herbert's early-down efficiency
confirming_evidence: on-time throws; positive early-down EPA; fewer late-down conversions required; low avoidable-sack rate
disconfirming_evidence: timing errors; stalled early downs; pressure or scrambling repeatedly breaks structure

preseason_hypothesis: Hampton will lead the backfield in carries routes and inside-10 opportunities
confirming_evidence: majority of first-unit carries; two-minute routes; goal-line work; stays on field across personnel groups
disconfirming_evidence: Vidal or Mitchell owns a separate drive package; Hampton leaves in passing situations; scoring work rotates

preseason_hypothesis: Mitchell will have a designed explosive-changeup package rather than only backup work
confirming_evidence: first-unit motion; outside runs; screens; touches scripted independently of Hampton rest
disconfirming_evidence: work occurs only with reserves or after Hampton exits; Vidal consistently works ahead of him

preseason_hypothesis: McConkey will lead Chargers receivers in routes and first-read targets
confirming_evidence: full-time 11-personnel role; motion and slot targets; third-down and two-minute priority
disconfirming_evidence: route rotation; Johnston or Harris leads first reads; McConkey leaves the field in core packages
review_trigger: first-unit preseason routes and first two regular-season games

preseason_hypothesis: Johnston and Harris will open as the primary perimeter pair while Thompson is a package player
confirming_evidence: Johnston and Harris lead outside routes; Thompson receives limited designed vertical and return work
disconfirming_evidence: Thompson earns full-time routes; another receiver displaces Johnston or Harris

preseason_hypothesis: Gadsden and Njoku will split receiving routes while Kolar leads inline blocking work
confirming_evidence: Gadsden and Njoku alternate or share route packages; Kolar aligns inline and blocks more often
disconfirming_evidence: one tight end dominates all first-unit routes; Kolar earns major receiving work; Gadsden or Njoku becomes a reserve
review_trigger: first-unit preseason routes and first two regular-season games

preseason_hypothesis: The Chargers will use 12 and 13 personnel without making run or pass intent obvious
confirming_evidence: multiple tight ends produce both runs and passes; motion changes strength; play action creates explosives
disconfirming_evidence: personnel grouping strongly predicts play type; 11 personnel overwhelmingly dominates
